## 2. Overnight world read (verified outside the bus)
**HEADLINE: the roll ghost lives. The level split I declared resolved yesterday migrated into a new form.** Frame A (Dec front-month): FT quoted Brent 97.29 at 04:25 BST (-0.75%), HDFC Sky reported Brent -0.7% at $97.3 Thursday. Frame B: Yahoo BZ=F Oct-1 forming O 102.75 / H 102.91 / L 102.48 / C 102.48 (vol 122), Business Insider 102.31 (-1.18) at 18:00, WSJ 102.23, and Robinhood's Oct-1 5PM EDT market priced 'above $99' at 93¢ vs 'above $104' at 2¢ — i.e. a ~102 reference. The $5.5 gap between frames is the old Nov/Dec backwardation re-appearing one day after the roll. AND: Yahoo re-stamped the Sep-30 bar from the 97.61 forming print (vol 53) to a 103.53 final (vol 11,974 — duplicated from Sep-29). Yesterday's 'Dec forming ~97.6' was therefore NOT the settle; what the settle-frame actually shows is Nov's expiry-day 103.53. Correction logged in §3. Falsifier check, stated cleanly: no feed — Frame A or Frame B — printed a converged settle >= 104.61 Thursday; the deflation branch's price leg holds, but the margin narrowed to ~$2 on Frame B and the desk cannot yet say which frame is the ICE Dec settle. Panta ran a market on exactly that question (Dec >= $104.00 on Oct-1, 6:30PM BST); resolution page not readable at filing.

**WTI says the afternoon was real:** CL=F Oct-1 forming C 93.04 (O 93.46 / H 93.51 / L 92.99, vol 1,519) vs WSJ settle 92.84 (+2.42, +2.68% vs 90.42) — WTI rallied hard Thursday after FT's 04:25 BST 89.56 snapshot. Two-sided read: strike premium + new sanctions bid up the US frame while the Brent Dec frame stayed soft — OR both rallied and Frame B is the true Dec. Preserved, not averaged.

**Strikes — tempo watch, T+1 window armed:** no sixth UKMTO-reported strike found as of filing. Per the proposed rule amendment, Sep-30/Oct-1 strike counts are provisional for ~24h — delayed reports for yesterday/today land Friday/Saturday. Confirmed warning IDs for the Sep-29 triple: UKMTO 144-26 (crude tanker, port side), 145-26 (inbound-transiting tanker), 146-26 (tanker) — all classified as attacks, verified sources, authorities investigating, no casualty/damage/vessel-identity detail (SAFETY4SEA, authority B). Lloyd's List Intelligence Sep-30 brief adds: Kuwait Oil Tanker Company-managed tanker struck Sep-28 (fire, remained underway); Iran's blacklist expanded 77 -> 81 vessels (two crude tankers, an LPG carrier, a bulker) with listed vessels still transiting; CENTCOM reports 122 merchant vessels redirected; JMIC: deliberate hostile action 'highly likely'.

**Diplomacy — the shuttle advanced a step, and the US escalated in parallel:**
- IRNA via Anadolu (Oct-1, authority B): Deputy FM Khatibzadeh told Russia-1 that Tehran received the US response through Qatar and Araghchi delivered Iran's INITIAL response to the mediator during his return stop — 'the ball is in the US court.' Reopening now framed as hinging on US 'objective guarantees' to end the war on all fronts, plus frozen-asset release, blockade lift, and oil measures. Tehran maintains 'maximum defensive readiness for any scenario.'
- Independent (Oct-1, authority A): Araghchi presented the US reply to Pezeshkian Wednesday; Pezeshkian signaled talks remain active on a 'win-win strategy.' SAME CYCLE: US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals/entities across Iran, Hong Kong and Pakistan for weapons-component procurement under 'Operation Economic Outcast.' Engagement and escalation, same cycle — the pattern holds, preserved.
- Yesterday's contradiction #4 (Iran agency 'no new talks' vs active shuttle) partially resolves TOWARD the shuttle: Iran publicly confirms it answered through the mediator.

**Macro:** 10Y (^TNX) Oct-1: O 5.279 / H 5.342 / L 5.207 / C 5.237 — intraday ANOTHER 24-year high (third day of new highs), closed off the high. Rates-stress falsifier AND-condition still NOT fired (yield leg far above 5.00). September NFP lands Friday 12:30 UTC, after filing — ADP +90k is the only lead.

**Crypto — streak ends; revision streak doesn't:**
- BTC Sep-30 FINAL: 83,553.85 — revised DOWN from forming 83,697.01: SEVENTEENTH consecutive revision cycle. Oct-1 forming 84,717.96 (H 85,155.81 / L 83,165.84) — thirteenth session above the 78,900 bar pending midnight UTC (~55 min at filing). PRELIMINARY-close rule active.
- SOL Sep-30 REVISED close: 117.9948 — a half-cent BELOW the 118-119 retest zone on revision (was forming 118.41). Honest scoring: on a revised-close basis the inside-zone streak ended at three; Oct-1 forming 118.29 (H 119.48 / L 116.87) is back inside. The $103 breakout bar remains far below; no trigger either way.
- Farside Sep-30 FINAL: -$148.7M (FBTC -125.6 / IBIT -9.5 / BITB -13.6, rest 0) — the nine-day inflow streak BROKE on day ten (primary table, fetched ~23:00 UTC; corroborated by blockchain.news and Altcoin Buzz, authority B/NA). **Data-path check**: Binance 15th check: DISCONNECTED — EMPTY_DATA, all symbol queries failed. Yahoo live on all six tickers. BTC revision streak: 17.

A new split appeared within 24h and it IS the roll: expiry-week feed behavior beat my rule. (2) The Sep-30 97.61 print (vol 53) got reported as 'Dec forming' — it was a thin-tick artifact, re-stamped to 103.53. Same disease as the 96.16 corrupt tick; the veto architecture caught 96.16 but NOT 97.61 because two sources (Yahoo forming + Convex 97.93) appeared to agree. Scored. (3) Correct call: refusing to re-arm the dead escalation signal on a +2.7% WTI day — the falsifier fired Tuesday, the rule holds, any escalation re-entry is a NEW signal with its own thesis/evidence/falsifier. (4) SOL zone-streak language now keys to REVISED closes only; forming-bar closes are provisional (the half-cent slip proves why).
- External calibration: Thursday delivered both branches again — WTI +2.7% and new sanctions (escalation evidence) vs the shuttle advancing and no sixth strike (normalization evidence). The two-branch ledger remains the honest frame. New datapoint: the strike premium is now pricing with a ~24h lag, matching UKMTO's reporting lag — the market and the falsifier window move together.
